title: Code-review radar for interviews (what seniors flag)
hook: Interview code review is a checklist in your head: async correctness, allocation hot paths, thread safety, API surface, nullability, and security at boundaries. This topic turns that radar into explicit signals interviewers listen for.

blocks.text: Code-review radar is the set of questions you ask on every pull request: Does this block the thread pool? Does it allocate in a loop? Is shared state synchronized? Are public types intentional? Are nullability warnings honest? Does SQS handler respect cancellation? Seniors trade off speed versus risk — they flag .Result, lock across await, and string concat in Redis paths immediately.

entries.plainDefinition: Blocking on Task.Result or .Wait() instead of awaiting.
entries.example: var data = GetDataAsync().Result; // starves thread pool

entries.plainDefinition: Message that always fails processing and must not infinite-retry.
entries.example: Malformed JSON — dead-letter after N attempts.

entries.plainDefinition: Code executed very frequently under production load.
entries.example: Redis cache read on every authenticated request.

blocks.text: System design interviews increasingly include 'review this code' slides. Naming the smell and the fix — single-flight cache, ConfigureAwait in library, IDisposable on native wrapper — demonstrates production experience. Radar connects modules 13–17 into one pass.

blocks.title: Review order
blocks.body: Correctness and security first, then concurrency, then allocations, then style.

snippet.explanation: Queue consumers must observe host cancellation for graceful drain.

snippet.label: Flags: nullable lie
snippet.explanation: Suppressing nullability with ! without guard is a review reject.

blocks.title: Review smells
rows: sync fs, busy loops on main thread

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Nitpicking naming while missing .Result on hot path. Approving public types without API check. Ignoring allocation in code that runs per message on SQS.

interviewTakeaways: Review correctness, concurrency, memory, API, security — in that priority.
Flag sync-over-async, lock across I/O, and allocation in loops immediately.
Connect smells to module fixes you already know.
commonPitfalls: Style comments without production risk assessment.
